title: K Divisible Elements Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums along with integers k and p, count the number of unique subarrays containing at most k elements divisible by p.
statement: Given an integer array nums along with integers k and p, count the number of unique subarrays containing at most k elements divisible by p. Two subarrays are distinct if they differ in length or at least one element.
constraints: A subarray is allowed when at most k of its elements are divisible by p.
Equal value sequences count once even when they occur at different positions.
hints: Enumerate a start index and extend its subarray until the divisible-element limit is exceeded.
Store each valid value sequence as an immutable tuple in a set.
For each left, append nums[right], update the divisible count, break above k, otherwise add tuple(current).
Every valid subarray is visited; invalid longer extensions cannot recover, and set identity implements the required value-based distinctness.
editorial: Every valid subarray is visited; invalid longer extensions cannot recover, and set identity implements the required value-based distinctness.

tests.explanation: Eleven distinct value sequences contain at most two even elements.
Every element is divisible by one, but k permits all ten subarrays and their sequences are distinct.
